Why identifying at-risk older adults matters — transition to stack layout, video appears top band

contentHints.title: Spotting who's at risk, early
contentHints.detail: Identifying older adults at risk is one of the most important things we can do to prevent abuse before it starts.

cards.intent: Personal risk factor 1 of 3 — mental illness or substance abuse

contentHints.title: Mental illness or substance abuse
contentHints.detail: Affecting either the older person, or the individual providing their care.

cards.intent: Personal risk factor 2 of 3 — cognitive and physical decline

contentHints.title: Cognitive & physical decline
contentHints.detail: Dementia, or physical and mental decline from chronic illness or stroke, raises risk.

cards.intent: Personal risk factor 3 of 3 — family history and stress

contentHints.title: Family history & stress
contentHints.detail: Transgenerational violence, ongoing family conflict, stress — even issues like gambling.

cards.intent: Warning sign — unchecked pressure escalates into abuse potential

contentHints.title: Left unchecked, it escalates
contentHints.detail: Personal and family pressures create environments where the potential for abuse can grow if unaddressed.

cards.intent: Relationship risk factor 1 of 2 — dependence and lost respect

contentHints.title: Dependence & lost respect
contentHints.detail: A lack of respect for older people, or a deep dependence between carer and older person, raises risk.

cards.intent: Warning sign — power imbalance is a red flag

contentHints.title: Any significant power imbalance
contentHints.detail: Care professionals must remain vigilant about power imbalance in the caring relationship.

cards.intent: Social risk factor — isolation reduces reporting

contentHints.title: Isolation silences reporting
contentHints.detail: Older people are often more socially isolated — making them less likely to report issues.

cards.intent: Organizational risk factor 1 of 4 — staffing and policy gaps

contentHints.title: Staffing & policy gaps
contentHints.detail: Inadequate staffing, skill mix, gaps in knowledge, and unclear policies all raise the risk of incidents.

cards.intent: Organizational risk factor 2 of 4 — poor response, management culture

contentHints.title: When leadership looks away
contentHints.detail: A poor response to allegations, or weak management, can create a culture where abuse goes unnoticed.

cards.intent: Organizational risk factor 3 of 4 — poor supervision and mentorship

contentHints.title: Unsupervised, unmentored staff
contentHints.detail: Poor supervision of inexperienced staff can lead to unintentional neglect or harmful practices.

cards.intent: Organizational risk factor 4 of 4 — demanding environments need support systems

contentHints.title: Support systems matter
contentHints.detail: Demanding clientele and high-stress environments need strong support to maintain the standard of care residents deserve.

cards.intent: Takeaway — count-up the 4 categories, ties everything together

contentHints.title: 4 categories. One goal: prevention.
contentHints.detail: Personal · Relationship · Social · Organizational — recognizing these factors early is a critical part of prevention.
